narrative.overview: Orch is a dual-register system. Marketing is dark and cinematic; product is light and precise. Operator Cobalt is the brand accent; success green is semantic only. Depth comes from a surface ladder and hairlines, not decorative shadows.
keyCharacteristics: Operator Cobalt accent ≤10% of product surfaces; success green is separate.
IBM Plex Sans/Mono with optical 600 display weight and tight tracking.
Surface ladder (paper → elevated → sunken) before shadow.
12–16px card radii; full pills on buttons.
Marketing aurora/blur motion allowed sparingly; product stays quiet.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Operator Cobalt is used on ≤10% of any given product screen.

rules.name: The Semantic Split Rule
rules.body: Primary action is cobalt; success is green. Do not conflate them.

rules.name: The Hairline First Rule
rules.body: Separation is hairline before tonal layering before shadow.

rules.name: The Mono For Truth Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono is reserved for what the system reports.

dos: Do use Operator Cobalt on primary actions, selection, and focus only.
Do walk the surface ladder before reaching for shadow.
Do use 12–16px radii on containers; pills on buttons.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion for all marketing motion.
donts: Don't use emerald as brand accent.
Don't ship flat zinc-only UI with no tonal depth.
Don't use AI-orb, gradient text, or identical icon-card grids.
Don't put an uppercase eyebrow on every section.
Don't pair 1px border with wide soft drop shadow as decoration.
